To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incorporation of a small proportion of nanofiller in epoxy resin improves the mechanical strength of the material, but the effect is more pronounced in the glassy state.

the incorporation of silica nanospheres into epoxy–amine networks leads to the improvement of the mechanical properties of the resulting nanocomposites, and that the best performance is obtained when using an intermediate proportion of filler.
the incorporation of silica nanoparticles in epoxy–amine networks increases the storage modulus of the materials in the glassy and rubber states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of nanocomposites based on epoxy resin reinforced with silica nanoparticles, with the aim of increasing the mechanical properties and improving their thermal resistance.
the preparation and characterisation of epoxy–silica nanocomposites, and the results obtained are in agreement with the conclusions of previous studies.
the study of the influence of the functional group of the silica nanospheres on the mechanical properties of the epoxy–silica nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best mechanical behaviour of the nanocomposites is observed for a percentage of 5 wt.%, and for a functionalised silica nanospheres with epoxy groups.
the use of functionalised nanospheres in epoxy matrix materials is a good strategy to increase the mechanical properties of the material.

the mechanical properties of epoxy matrix–silica nanocomposites are strongly dependent on the nature of the functional groups of the silica nanospheres and on the proportion of the filler in the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical properties of epoxy–silica nanocomposites are improved with the addition of silica nanospheres.
the best mechanical behaviour of the epoxy matrix–silica nanocomposites is observed in materials with an intermediate proportion (5–7 wt.%) of silica nanospheres with epoxy groups.

the best mechanical properties are achieved in the systems where the strengthening material is silica nanospheres with epoxy groups, and that these properties are achieved with a proportion of strengthening material of 5–7wt.%.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of silica nanospheres in the epoxy matrix, functionalised with epoxy or amine groups, can improve the mechanical properties of the material in both glassy (up to 5 wt.% strengthening substance) and rubbery states (up to 7 wt.% strengthening substance).

the incorporation of silica nanoparticles into the epoxy matrix can improve the mechanical properties of the material, and this effect is enhanced if the nanoparticles are functionalised with epoxy or amine groups.

the use of functionalised nanospheres in epoxy matrix composites improves their mechanical properties, as reflected in the storage shear modulus, and that the best performance is observed in those systems where the silica particles are functionalised with epoxy or amine groups.
